title: Hut to Hut in the Alps: A First-Timer’s Guide
text: Planning your first hut-to-hut walk in the Alps? Learn when to book, what to pack and why to start early to beat afternoon storms.
article:
Hut to Hut in the Alps: A First-Timer’s Guide

Excerpt: Booking, packing and pacing for your first multi-day walk between mountain huts.

Walking from hut to hut is the easiest way to spend a week in the high mountains without carrying a tent. You sleep in dormitories, eat what the warden cooks, and set off again after breakfast. Booking Most huts open from late June to mid September. Book at least two months ahead for weekends in July and August, and always tell the hut if you cancel: they will send someone looking for you if you don’t arrive. What to pack A sleeping-bag liner (required in most huts) Hut shoes or light sandals Cash: many huts don’t take cards Half board usually costs €60–80 a night Waterproofs, even if the forecast is clear Start early, finish early. Afternoon storms are the rule in July, not the exception. We’ve put our favourite four-day loop in a separate guide: four days above Chamonix .

title: Four Days Above Chamonix
text: A four-day hut loop from Les Houches to Chamonix, with distance and ascent for each day and a way around the ladders and chains on day two.
article:
Four Days Above Chamonix

This loop links four huts on the south side of the valley. It needs a head for heights on day two and nothing technical otherwise. Day Route Distance Ascent 1 Les Houches to Refuge de Bellachat 9 km 1,150 m 2 Bellachat to Lac Blanc 14 km 900 m 3 Lac Blanc to Refuge de la Charlanon 8 km 350 m 4 Charlanon to Chamonix 11 km 200 m Day two crosses a section with ladders and fixed chains. If that isn’t for you, drop down to the valley and take the lift up again. For booking and packing, see our first-timer’s guide .

title: Interrail on a Budget: 10 Things We Learned
text: Ten lessons from a month of Interrail travel around Europe on a tight budget, from buying the pass in a sale to skipping high-speed reservations and taking night trains.
article:
Interrail on a Budget: 10 Things We Learned

Excerpt: How to make a rail pass go further.

A month of trains around Europe, spending as little as we could. Here’s what made the difference. Buy the pass in a sale. They come round twice a year. Pick a flexi pass with fewer travel days than you think you need. Avoid high-speed trains in France, Italy and Spain: reservations cost extra. Regional trains are often free with the pass and only a little slower. Night trains save a night of accommodation. Bring a refillable bottle and a picnic. Stations with left-luggage lockers let you see a city between trains. Book hostels with kitchens. Many city museums are free on the first Sunday of the month. Don’t try to see everything. Two nights per stop is plenty.

title: Porto’s Bolhão Market Reopens
text: Porto's Bolhão market has reopened after four years of restoration: when to go, what to find at the stalls, and where to eat lunch upstairs.
article:
Porto’s Bolhão Market Reopens

Excerpt: After four years of restoration, the city’s market hall is back.

Porto’s Bolhão market reopened in September after four years of restoration. The iron roof is the original, cleaned and repaired; the stalls are new, and many of the old traders are back. Go on a weekday morning for fish, flowers and the best people-watching in the city. There’s a row of small restaurants on the upper level if you want lunch with a view of the stalls. Open Monday to Saturday, 8am to 8pm.

title: Why We Stopped Flying Short-Haul
text: An editor's note on why the team stopped taking flights under 1,000 km for stories, and how slower train journeys made trips longer and better.
article:
Why We Stopped Flying Short-Haul

Excerpt: An editor’s note on slower trips.

Two years ago the editorial team agreed to stop taking flights under 1,000 km for our stories. This is what changed. Trips got longer, and they got better. On the train you arrive in the middle of a city instead of at its edge, and the journey becomes part of the story rather than a gap in it. It is not always possible, and we still fly when there is no reasonable alternative. But “reasonable” turned out to cover a lot more than we expected. Editor's note: our Interrail budget guide is a good place to start.

title: Sydney Harbour by Ferry
text: Skip the tour boats: the thirty-minute public ferry from Circular Quay to Manly passes the Opera House and the harbour heads for a few dollars.
article:
Sydney Harbour by Ferry

Excerpt: The cheapest harbour cruise in the world is a commuter ferry.

Skip the tour boats. The public ferry from Circular Quay to Manly takes thirty minutes, passes the Opera House and the harbour heads, and costs a few dollars with a transport card. Go late in the afternoon, sit outside on the left going out, and stay for dinner in Manly. The last boats run until around midnight. On Sundays fares are capped for the whole day, so it is the day to ride every route.

title: Marrakech’s Souks Without the Stress
text: Practical tips for the souks north of Jemaa el-Fnaa: when to go, how to agree on prices, and how to find your way out of the maze.
article:
Marrakech’s Souks Without the Stress

Excerpt: How to enjoy the markets of the medina.

The souks north of Jemaa el-Fnaa are a maze on purpose. Getting lost is part of the visit; the trick is to enjoy it. Go in the morning, before the heat and the crowds. Agree on a price before anything is wrapped, and walk away politely if it is too high: you will usually be called back. When you want to find your way out, follow the flow of people downhill towards the main square.

title: How to Order Coffee in Vienna
text: Melange, Einspänner or Verlängerter? Learn what to order in a Viennese coffee house, and why nobody will rush you to leave.
article:
How to Order Coffee in Vienna

Excerpt: A Melange is not a cappuccino, and nobody will rush you.

A Viennese coffee house sells time as much as coffee. Order, and you can stay for hours with the newspapers. Melange : espresso with steamed milk and foam. Einspänner : black coffee under whipped cream, served in a glass. Verlängerter : espresso lengthened with hot water. Every coffee comes with a glass of water. When it is refilled without asking, you are welcome to stay.

title: Could You Go From Lisbon to Tokyo by Train?
text: We tried to plan a train trip from Lisbon to Tokyo through Europe, Central Asia and China, and found out why it can't be done this year.
article:
Could You Go From Lisbon to Tokyo by Train?

Excerpt: In theory yes; in practice, not this year.

On a map the route looks almost continuous: across Europe, then east through Central Asia and China, and a ferry to Japan at the end. In practice several border crossings have no passenger trains, and some services need visas weeks in advance. We tried to plan it and gave up at the third missing connection. If you want a long train journey this year, pick one continent and do it properly.

title: Table Mountain: Cable Car or On Foot?
text: How to choose between the cable car and the steep Platteklip Gorge path up Table Mountain, with tips on timing, queues and the weather.
article:
Table Mountain: Cable Car or On Foot?

The cable car reaches the top of Table Mountain in a few minutes. The Platteklip Gorge path takes two to three hours and climbs steeply the whole way. Walk up in the cool of the morning and ride down in the afternoon, when the queues for the descent are short. Check the weather first: when the cloud the locals call the tablecloth sits on the summit, the cable car stops and the views disappear.

Einspänner : black coffee under whipped cream, served in a glass. Verlängerter : espresso lengthened with hot water. Every coffee comes with a glass of water. When it is refilled without asking, you are welcome to stay.

faithful.reason: The summary makes claims about coffee generally and travels worldwide, not about the Vienna article's content; it invents no specific facts but is not supported by the article's details.

specific.reason: It could be pasted onto any travel article about coffee anywhere; it mentions no Vienna, coffee house, or specific drinks.

plain.reason: The tone is calm with no hype, exclamation marks, or clickbait, though 'great coffee' is mildly promotional.

purpose.reason: It gestures at the topic but does not tell the reader what they will learn from the article (Viennese coffee types, ordering customs), so it fails to do the summary's job.

title: Sydney Harbour by Ferry
text: A simple tip for seeing a famous city from the water without spending much.
article:
Sydney Harbour by Ferry

Excerpt: The cheapest harbour cruise in the world is a commuter ferry.

Skip the tour boats. The public ferry from Circular Quay to Manly takes thirty minutes, passes the Opera House and the harbour heads, and costs a few dollars with a transport card. Go late in the afternoon, sit outside on the left going out, and stay for dinner in Manly. The last boats run until around midnight. On Sundays fares are capped for the whole day, so it is the day to ride every route.

faithful.reason: The summary says it's a tip for seeing the city from the water cheaply, which the article supports (commuter ferry, a few dollars). It invents no facts.

specific.reason: It is vague: 'a famous city' and 'a simple tip' could describe many travel articles. It does not mention Sydney Harbour, the ferry to Manly, or the Opera House.

plain.reason: The tone is calm and plain, with no hype, superlatives, or exclamation marks.

purpose.reason: It is one sentence that tells the reader the article offers a cheap way to see a city from the water. That is a reasonable summary of what they will get, though it lacks concrete detail about the route.

title: Table Mountain: Cable Car or On Foot?
text: The MOST breathtaking climb on the planet!!! Table Mountain will blow your mind, cable car or not.
article:
Table Mountain: Cable Car or On Foot?

The cable car reaches the top of Table Mountain in a few minutes. The Platteklip Gorge path takes two to three hours and climbs steeply the whole way. Walk up in the cool of the morning and ride down in the afternoon, when the queues for the descent are short. Check the weather first: when the cloud the locals call the tablecloth sits on the summit, the cable car stops and the views disappear.

faithful.reason: The text claims the climb is the most breathtaking on the planet and that the mountain will blow your mind, which the article does not support; it only describes logistics and a cloud that obscures views.

specific.reason: It mentions Table Mountain and the cable car, so it is tied to this article, though the content is generic hype that could fit many mountain pieces.

plain.reason: It uses superlatives, all-caps, multiple exclamation marks and hype language like blow your mind, the opposite of plain and calm.

purpose.reason: As an SEO description it is a single sentence-like blurb, but it does not convey what the article covers (cable car versus Platteklip path, timing, weather) and so gives a searcher little reason to click beyond vague hype.

title: Eating Well in Hanoi
text: Hanoi eats on the pavement. Each stall makes one dish. Start with pho, then bun cha, then egg coffee in the Old Quarter.
article:
Eating Well in Hanoi

Excerpt: Pho, and much more.

Hanoi eats on the pavement. Most of the best food in the city is cooked at stalls with plastic stools, and each stall makes one dish. Start the day with pho, have bun cha for lunch, and end with egg coffee in the Old Quarter. Look for the stalls where locals are queuing and point at what they are having.

specific.reason: Names Hanoi dishes and the Old Quarter, so it is about this article and not pasteable onto another travel piece.

plain.reason: Calm, declarative sentences with no hype, superlatives, exclamation marks or clichés.

purpose.reason: As an SEO description it is three sentences rather than a single sentence, so it does not meet the one-sentence format; it does hint at the content but is not a single click-inducing line.

title: Marrakech’s Souks Without the Stress
text: Marrakech.
article:
Marrakech’s Souks Without the Stress

Excerpt: How to enjoy the markets of the medina.

The souks north of Jemaa el-Fnaa are a maze on purpose. Getting lost is part of the visit; the trick is to enjoy it. Go in the morning, before the heat and the crowds. Agree on a price before anything is wrapped, and walk away politely if it is too high: you will usually be called back. When you want to find your way out, follow the flow of people downhill towards the main square.

faithful.reason: The text is just the word 'Marrakech', which is a place the article covers, so it invents nothing.

specific.reason: A single city name is too generic; it could sit atop any Marrakech article and says nothing about souks or the advice given.

plain.reason: It is plain and calm with no hype, superlatives, or clichés.

purpose.reason: A summary should tell the reader what they will get in one or two sentences; a bare city name tells them nothing about the content or benefit.
